&#8220;Operating lease liabilities&#8221; and &#8220;Long-term operating</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">lease liabilities&#8221; in</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">the</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheet</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">s</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> as of December 31, </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2020 and </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2019. The Company has </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000686" name="us-gaap:FinanceLeaseLiability" contextRef="C_0001010612_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3">no</ix:nonFraction></span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> finance leases.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Lease terms for the Company&#8217;s leases are generally <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000687" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract" contextRef="C_0001010612_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen" continuedAt="C_9e2cd8cb-de01-435b-91c0-f9d6ebd7a533">three</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000688" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract" contextRef="C_0001010612_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">20<ix:continuation id="C_9e2cd8cb-de01-435b-91c0-f9d6ebd7a533"> years</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric> with renewal options typically ranging from <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000689" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRenewalTerm" contextRef="C_0001010612_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">one month</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000690" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRenewalTerm" contextRef="C_0001010612_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">five years</ix:nonNumeric> and largely require the Company to pay a proportionate share of real estate taxes, insurance, common area maintenance, and other operating costs in addition to a base or fixed rent. The Company's operating leases have remaining lease terms of <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000691" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRemainingLeaseTerm" contextRef="C_0001010612_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">one month</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000692" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRemainingLeaseTerm" contextRef="C_0001010612_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">12 years</ix:nonNumeric> as of December 31, 2020.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s leases do not contain any material residual value guarantees or material restrictive covenants.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company subleases certain of its facilities that have been abandoned before the expiration of the lease term.&#160;&#160;Operating lease costs on abandoned facilities are reduced by sublease income and included in &#8220;General and administrative&#8221; costs in the accompanying Consolidated Statements of Operations. The Company&#8217;s sublease arrangements do not contain renewal options or restrictive covenants. The Company&#8217;s subleases have varying remaining lease terms extending through 2025, and future contractual sublease payments are expected to be $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000693" name="syke:ExpectedFutureContractualSubleaseIncome" contextRef="C_0001010612_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">9.3</ix:nonFraction> million over the remaining lease terms.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000477" name="us-gaap:LeaseCostTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001010612_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000477_cnt_1">

The TMC Purchase Agreement contained customary representations and warranties, indemnification obligations and covenants.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has reflected Symphony&#8217;s results in its consolidated financial statements in the EMEA segment since November 1, 2018.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">WhistleOut Acquisition</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On July 9, 2018, the Company, as guarantor, and its wholly-owned subsidiaries, Sykes Australia Pty Ltd, an Australian company, and Clear Link Technologies, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, entered into and closed a definitive Share Sale Agreement (the &#8220;WhistleOut Sale Agreement&#8221;) with WhistleOut Nominees Pty Ltd as trustee for the WhistleOut Holdings Unit Trust, CPC Investments USA Pty Ltd, JJZL Pty Ltd, Kenneth Wong as trustee for Wong Family Trust and C41 Pty Ltd as trustee for the Ottery Family Trust to acquire all of the outstanding shares of WhistleOut Pty Ltd and WhistleOut, Inc. (together, &#8220;WhistleOut&#8221;). The WhistleOut Sale Agreement contained customary representations and warranties, indemnification obligations and covenants.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The aggregate purchase price of AUD <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217AUD" id="F_000758" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferred1" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_sykeWhistleOutMember_20180709_20180709" decimals="-5" scale="6">30.2</ix:nonFraction> million ($<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000759" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferred1" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_sykeWhistleOutMember_20180709_20180709" decimals="-5" scale="6">22.4</ix:nonFraction> million) was paid at the closing of the transaction on <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000760" name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionEffectiveDateOfAcquisition1" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_sykeWhistleOutMember_20180709_20180709" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">July 9, 2018</ix:nonNumeric>. Subsequent to the finalization of the working capital adjustments during the quarter ended March 31, 2019, the purchase price was adjusted to AUD <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217AUD" id="F_000761" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferred1" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_sykeWhistleOutMember_20190101_20190331" decimals="-5" scale="6">30.3</ix:nonFraction> million ($<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000762" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferred1" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_sykeWhistleOutMember_20190101_20190331" decimals="-5" scale="6">22.5</ix:nonFraction> million). The purchase price was funded through $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000763" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfLongTermDebt" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_sykeWhistleOutMember_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20180709_20180709" decimals="-5" scale="6">22.0</ix:nonFraction> million of additional borrowings under the Company&#8217;s credit agreement. The WhistleOut Sale Agreement provided for a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000765">three-year</span>, retention based earnout of AUD <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217AUD" id="F_000766" name="syke:BusinessAcquisitionEarnOut" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_sykeWhistleOutMember_20180709_20180709" decimals="-5" scale="6">14.0</ix:nonFraction> million payable in <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000764" name="syke:BusinessAcquisitionEarnoutPaymentTerms" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_sykeWhistleOutMember_20190101_20191231">three installments on or about July 1, 2019, 2020 and 2021</ix:nonNumeric>.&#160;&#160;The Company paid the first installment of the earn-out of AUD <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217AUD" id="F_000767" name="syke:PaymentForBusinessAcquisitionEarnOut" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_sykeWhistleOutMember_20190701_20190731" decimals="-5" scale="6">6.0</ix:nonFraction> million ($<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000768" name="syke:PaymentForBusinessAcquisitionEarnOut" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_sykeWhistleOutMember_20190701_20190731" decimals="-5" scale="6">4.2</ix:nonFraction> million) in July 2019.&#160;&#160;The Company accelerated the 2021 installment of the retention bonus and paid AUD <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217AUD" id="F_000769" name="syke:PaymentForBusinessAcquisitionEarnOut" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_sykeWhistleOutMember_20200701_20200731" decimals="-5" scale="6">8.0</ix:nonFraction> million ($<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000770" name="syke:PaymentForBusinessAcquisitionEarnOut" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_sykeWhistleOutMember_20200701_20200731" decimals="-5" scale="6">5.6</ix:nonFraction> million) in July 2020, which represented both the 2020 and 2021 installments. <p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000420" name="us-gaap:RestructuringAndRelatedActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001010612_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000420_dcnt_8800263d-120e-4471-9721-4e11f4d5b597">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 5. Costs Associated with Exit or Disposal Activities</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Americas 2019 Exit Plan</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the first quarter of 2019, the Company initiated a restructuring plan to simplify and refine its operating model in the U.S. (the &#8220;Americas 2019 Exit Plan&#8221;), in part to improve agent attrition and absenteeism. The Americas 2019 Exit Plan included closing customer experience management centers, consolidating leased space in various locations in the U.S. and management reorganization. The Company finalized the actions as of September 30, 2019. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Americas 2018 Exit Plan</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the second quarter of 2018, the Company initiated a restructuring plan to manage and optimize capacity utilization, which included closing customer experience management centers and consolidating leased space in various locations in the U.S. and Canada (the &#8220;Americas 2018 Exit Plan&#8221;). The Company finalized the site closures under the Americas 2018 Exit Plan as of December 31, 2018, resulting in a reduction of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_sykeSeat" id="F_000774" name="syke:RestructuringAndRelatedCostNumberOfSeatsEliminatedInceptionToDate" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapRestructuringPlanAxis_sykeAmericas2018ExitPlanMember_us-gaapStatementBusinessSegmentsAxis_sykeAmericasSegmentMember_20181231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">5,000</ix:nonFraction> seats. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s actions under both the Americas 2018 and 2019 Exit Plans resulted in general and administrative cost savings and lower depreciation expense.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000479" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfRestructuringAndRelatedCostsTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001010612_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000479_dcnt_f88679c1-0cb2-4d6c-811e-b0ef5dde1688">

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Non-Recurring Fair Value</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Certain assets are not required to be measured at fair value on a recurring basis and are reported at their carrying values, including goodwill, other intangible assets, other long-lived assets, ROU assets and equity method investments. The carrying value of these assets is evaluated for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount may not be recoverable (and at least annually for goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible assets), and if applicable, written down to fair value.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company is reevaluating its real estate footprint in connection with a shift of a portion of its workforce to a permanent remote working environment in both the Americas and EMEA and transitioned <span style="color:#000000;">approximately <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_sykeSeat" id="F_000924" name="syke:NumberOfSeatsTransitionedToAtHome" contextRef="C_0001010612_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">3,200</ix:nonFraction> seats from brick and mortar to at home agents</span>. The Company decided to terminate, sublease or abandon leases prior to the end of their lease terms at certain of its sites and recorded impairment losses during the year ended December 31, 2020 related to the exit of leased facilities and the leasehold improvements, equipment, furniture and fixtures located in these sites which were not recoverable. As the fair value of the ROU assets was less than the carrying value, the Company recognized an impairment of ROU assets, reducing the carrying value of the ROU assets to an estimated fair value of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000925" name="syke:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAssetFairValueDisclosure" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapFairValueByFairValueHierarchyLevelAxis_us-gaapFairValueInputsLevel2Member_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">11.7</ix:nonFraction> million. The fair value of the ROU assets where the Company intends to sublease was estimated using Level 2 inputs such as market comparables to estimate future cash flows expected from sublease income over the remaining lease terms. Further changes in the estimated amount or timing of cash flows from sublease arrangements could result in additional impairment charges. The impairment of property and equipment reduced the carrying amount of the applicable assets to their fair value of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000926" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentFairValueDisclosure" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapFairValueByFairValueHierarchyLevelAxis_us-gaapFairValueInputsLevel2Member_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.6</ix:nonFraction> million, which was estimated using Level 2 inputs such as appraisals, market prices of comparable assets, or independent third party offers.</p>

See Note 5, Costs Associated with Exit or Disposal Activities, for further information.</p>

<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;color:#auto;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;letter-spacing:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;"><span style="Background-color:#auto;text-decoration:none;"></span><span style="color:#000000;"></span><span style="font-size:8.5pt;color:#000000;">See Note 7, Goodwill and Intangible Assets, for further information.&#160;&#160;The year ended December 31, 2020 includes the impairment of a portion of the Symphony reporting unit&#8217;s goodwill.</span></p></td></tr></table></div></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company performs its annual goodwill impairment test during the third quarter, or more frequently if indicators of impairment exist. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">For the annual goodwill impairment test, the Company elected to forgo the option to first assess qualitative factors and performed its annual quantitative goodwill impairment test as of July 31, 2020. Under ASC 350, the carrying value of assets is calculated at the reporting unit level. <span style="color:#000000;">The quantitative assessment of goodwill includes comparing a reporting unit&#8217;s calculated fair value to its carrying value. The calculation of fair value requires significant judgments including estimation of future cash flows, which is dependent on internal forecasts, estimation of the projected long-term growth rate and determination of the Company&#8217;s weighted average cost of capital. Changes in these estimates and assumptions could materially affect the determination of fair value and/or conclusions on goodwill impairment for each reporting unit. </span>If the fair value of the reporting unit is less than its carrying value, goodwill is considered impaired and an impairment loss is recognized for the amount by which the carrying value exceeds the reporting unit&#8217;s fair value, not to exceed the total amount of goodwill allocated to that reporting unit.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The process of evaluating the fair value of the reporting units is highly subjective and requires significant judgment and estimates as the reporting units operate in a number of markets and geographical regions. The Company considered the income and market approaches to determine its best estimates of fair value, which incorporated the following significant assumptions: </p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Clearlink, Latin America and Qelp reporting units&#8217; <span style="color:#000000;">fair value exceeded their respective carrying values, although the fair value cushion was not substantial</span>. The increase in the cushion from the prior year for the Qelp reporting unit was primarily attributable to an increase in the multiples applied using the guideline public company method under the market approach valuation. The decrease in the cushion from the prior year for the Latin America reporting unit was primarily attributable to an increase in its WACC driven by an increase in the country risk premium, market risk premium and country default spread. <span style="color:#000000;">The Clearlink, Latin America </span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deferred gains (losses) and other future reclassifications from AOCI will fluctuate with movements in the underlying market price of the forward contracts and options as well as the related settlement of forecasted transactions.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Non-Designated Hedges</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Foreign Currency Contracts</span><span style="font-weight:bold;"> </span><span style="font-style:normal;">&#8211;</span><span style="font-weight:bold;"> </span><span style="font-style:normal;">The Company also periodically enters into foreign currency hedge contracts that are not designated as hedges as defined under ASC 815. The purpose of these derivative instruments is to protect the Company&#8217;s interests against adverse foreign currency moves relating primarily to intercompany receivables and payables, and other assets and liabilities that are denominated in currencies other than the Company&#8217;s subsidiaries&#8217; functional currencies. See Note 1, Overview and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies, for additional </span></p>
</ix:nonNumeric><p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">82</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" /><ix:continuation id="F_000427_dcnt_3d01ac09-6034-40d4-abfb-aa40ab37fbc0" continuedAt="F_000427_dcnt_4d472c2a-2434-4f6b-a7a4-03fae498d378">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-style:normal;">information on the Company&#8217;s purpose for </span><span style="font-style:normal;">entering into</span><span style="font-style:normal;"> derivatives not designated as hedging instruments and its overall risk management strategies</span><span style="color:#000000;font-style:normal;">.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Embedded Derivatives</span><span style="font-style:normal;"> &#8211; </span><span style="color:#000000;font-style:normal;">The Company enters into c</span><span style="font-style:normal;">ertain lease agreements which require payments not denominated in the functional currency of any substantial party to the agreements. Prior to the adoption of ASC 842 on January 1, 2019, the foreign currency component of these contracts met the criteria under ASC 815 as embedded derivatives. The Company determined that the embedded derivatives were not clearly and closely related to the economic characteristics and risks of the host contracts (lease agreements), and separate, stand-alone instruments with the same terms as the embedded derivative instruments would otherwise qualify as derivative instruments, thereby requiring separation from the lease agreements and recognition at fair value. Such instruments do not qualify for hedge accounting under ASC 815. The Company&#8217;s embedded derivatives were derecognized on January 1, 2019.</span></p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000493" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfNotionalAmountsOfOutstandingDerivativePositionsTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001010612_20200101_20201231" escape="true">

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On February 14, 2019, the Company entered into a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001234" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_sykeTwoThousandNineteenCreditAgreementMember_20190214" decimals="INF" scale="6">500</ix:nonFraction> million senior revolving credit facility (the &#8220;2019 Credit Agreement&#8221;) with a group of lenders, KeyBank National Association, as Administrative Agent, Swing Line Lender and Issuing Lender (&#8220;KeyBank&#8221;), the lenders named therein, and KeyBanc Capital Markets Inc. as Lead Arranger and Sole Book Runner. The 2019 Credit Agreement replaced the Company&#8217;s previous $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001235" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_sykeTwoThousandFifteenCreditAgreementMember_20150512" decimals="INF" scale="6">440</ix:nonFraction> million revolving credit facility dated May 12, 2015 (the &#8220;2015 Credit Agreement&#8221;), which agreement was terminated simultaneous with entering into the 2019 Credit Agreement. The 2019 Credit Agreement is subject to certain borrowing limitations and includes certain customary financial and restrictive covenants.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The 2019 Credit Agreement includes a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001236" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_sykeAlternateCurrencySubFacilityMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_sykeTwoThousandNineteenCreditAgreementMember_20190214" decimals="INF" scale="6">200</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million alternate-currency sub-facility, a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001237" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_sykeSwinglineSubFacilityMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_sykeTwoThousandNineteenCreditAgreementMember_20190214" decimals="INF" scale="6">15</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million swingline sub-facility and a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001238" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapLetterOfCreditMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_sykeTwoThousandNineteenCreditAgreementMember_20190214" decimals="INF" scale="6">15</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million letter of credit sub-facility, and may be used for general corporate purposes including acquisitions, share repurchases, working capital support and letters of credit, subject to certain limitations.&#160;&#160;The Company is not currently aware of any inability of its lenders to provide access to the full commitment of funds that exist under the revolving credit facility, if necessary.&#160;&#160;However, there can be no assurance that such facility will be available to the Company, even though it is a binding commitment of the financial institutions.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The 2019 Credit Agreement matures on <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001239" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityExpirationDate1" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_sykeTwoThousandNineteenCreditAgreementMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">February 14, 2024</ix:nonNumeric>, and had outstanding borrowings of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001240" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebtNoncurrent" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_sykeTwoThousandNineteenCreditAgreementMember_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">63.0</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001241" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebtNoncurrent" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_sykeTwoThousandNineteenCreditAgreementMember_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">73.0</ix:nonFraction> million at December 31, 2020 and 2019, respectively, included in &#8220;Long-term debt&#8221; in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company provides U.S. income taxes on the earnings of foreign subsidiaries unless they are exempted from taxation. During the fourth quarter of 2019, we partially reversed our permanent reinvestment assertion in connection with plans to distribute cash from certain of our foreign subsidiaries in 2020 or subsequent years.&#160;&#160;In connection with this change in assertion, the Company recorded $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001441" name="syke:IncomeTaxReconciliationChangeInAssertion" contextRef="C_0001010612_20191001_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">1.0</ix:nonFraction> million of withholding tax. No additional income taxes have been provided for any remaining reinvested earnings or outside basis differences inherent in these entities as these amounts continue to be indefinitely reinvested in foreign operations. Determining the amount of unrecognized deferred tax liability related to any remaining outside basis difference in these entities is not practicable due to the inherent complexity of the multi-jurisdictional tax environment in which the Company operates.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has been granted tax holidays in the Philippines, Colombia, Costa Rica and El Salvador, some of which have various expiration dates ranging from <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001442" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxHolidayTerminationDate" contextRef="C_0001010612_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20200101_20201231">2021</ix:nonNumeric> through <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001443" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxHolidayTerminationDate" contextRef="C_0001010612_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20200101_20201231">2030</ix:nonNumeric>. In some cases, the tax holidays expire without possibility of renewal. In other cases, the Company expects to renew these tax holidays, but there are no assurances from the respective foreign governments that they will either renew them on the same or similar terms or that the law and regulations relating to the holiday will remain the same. This could potentially result in future adverse tax consequences in the local jurisdiction, the impact of which is not practicable to estimate due to the inherent complexity of estimating critical variables such as long-term future profitability, tax regulations and rates in the multi-jurisdictional tax environment in which the Company operates. The Company&#8217;s tax holidays decreased the provision for income taxes by $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001444" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxReconciliationTaxHolidays" contextRef="C_0001010612_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">3.8</ix:nonFraction> million ($<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_001447" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxHolidayIncomeTaxBenefitsPerShare" contextRef="C_0001010612_20200101_20201231" decimals="2">0.09</ix:nonFraction> per diluted share), $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001445" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxReconciliationTaxHolidays" contextRef="C_0001010612_20190101_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">3.1</ix:nonFraction> million ($<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_001448" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxHolidayIncomeTaxBenefitsPerShare" contextRef="C_0001010612_20190101_20191231" decimals="2">0.07</ix:nonFraction> per diluted share) and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001446" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxReconciliationTaxHolidays" contextRef="C_0001010612_20180101_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">4.1</ix:nonFraction> million ($<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_001449" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxHolidayIncomeTaxBenefitsPerShare" contextRef="C_0001010612_20180101_20181231" decimals="2">0.10</ix:nonFraction> per diluted share) for the years ended December 31, 2020, 2019 and 2018, respectively.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Indemnities, Commitments and Guarantees</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">From time to time, during the normal course of business, the Company may make certain indemnities, commitments and guarantees under which it may be required to make payments in relation to certain transactions. These include but are not limited to: (i) indemnities to clients, vendors and service providers pertaining to claims based on negligence or willful misconduct of the Company and (ii) indemnities involving breach of contract, the accuracy of representations and warranties of the Company, or other liabilities assumed by the Company in certain contracts. In addition, the Company has agreements whereby it will indemnify certain officers and directors for certain events or occurrences while the officer or director is, or was, serving at the Company&#8217;s request in such capacity. The indemnification period covers all pertinent events and occurrences during the officer&#8217;s or director&#8217;s lifetime. The maximum potential amount of future payments the Company could be required to make under these indemnification agreements is unlimited&#59; however, the Company has director and officer insurance coverage that limits its exposure and enables it to recover a portion of any future amounts paid. The Company believes the applicable insurance coverage is generally adequate to cover any estimated potential liability under these indemnification agreements. The majority of these indemnities, commitments and guarantees do not provide for any limitation of the maximum potential for future payments the Company could be obligated to make. The Company has not recorded any liability for these indemnities, commitments and guarantees in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Company has some client contracts that do not contain contractual provisions for the limitation of liability, and other client contracts that contain agreed upon exceptions to limitation of liability.&#160;&#160;The Company has not recorded any liability in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets with respect to any client contracts under which the Company has or may have unlimited liability.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Loss Contingencies</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company received a state audit assessment and is currently rebutting the position. The Company has determined that the likelihood of a liability is reasonably possible and developed a range of possible loss up to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001559" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyEstimateOfPossibleLoss" contextRef="C_0001010612_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="6">1.8</ix:nonFraction> million, net of federal benefit.</p>
</ix:nonNumeric><p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">93</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company, from time to time, is involved in legal actions arising in the ordinary course of business.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001560" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyLawsuitFilingDate" contextRef="C_0001010612_srtLitigationCaseAxis_sykeSlaughterLawsuitMember_20200101_20201231">August 24, 2017</ix:nonNumeric>, a collective action lawsuit was filed against the Company in the United States District Court for the District of Colorado (the &#8220;Court&#8221;), Slaughter v. Sykes Enterprises, Inc., Case No. 17 Civ. 2038. The lawsuit claimed that the Company failed to pay certain employees overtime compensation for the hours they worked over forty in a workweek, as required by the Fair Labor Standards Act.&#160;&#160;On <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001561" name="syke:LitigationVerbalSettlementAgreementDate" contextRef="C_0001010612_srtLitigationCaseAxis_sykeSlaughterLawsuitMember_20200101_20201231">October 17, 2018</ix:nonNumeric>, the parties entered into a verbal agreement to fully resolve all claims and the fees for the plaintiffs&#8217; attorneys for a total payment of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001562" name="syke:LitigationVerbalSettlementAgreement" contextRef="C_0001010612_srtLitigationCaseAxis_sykeSlaughterLawsuitMember_20181017_20181017" decimals="-5" scale="6">1.2</ix:nonFraction> million. The settlement agreement was approved by the Court and a charge of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001563" name="syke:LitigationChargesInPeriod" contextRef="C_0001010612_srtLitigationCaseAxis_sykeSlaughterLawsuitMember_us-gaapIncomeStatementLocationAxis_us-gaapGeneralAndAdministrativeExpenseMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">1.2</ix:nonFraction> million was included in &#8220;General and administrative&#8221; in the accompanying Consolidated Statement of Operations for the year ended December 31, 2018.&#160;&#160;The settlement was paid in full on December 31, 2018.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">With respect to any such other currently pending matters, management believes that the Company has adequate legal defenses and/or, when possible and appropriate, has provided adequate accruals related to those matters such that the ultimate outcome will not have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000438" name="us-gaap:PensionAndOtherPostretirementBenefitsDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001010612_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000438_dcnt_985682ea-4e5e-4d09-b6a5-2404615fae0d">

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company evaluates these assumptions on a periodic basis taking into consideration current market conditions and historical market data. The discount rate is used to calculate expected future cash flows at a present value on the measurement date, which is December 31. This rate represents the market rate for high-quality fixed income investments. A lower discount rate would increase the present value of benefit obligations. Other assumptions include demographic factors such as attrition, mortality, and disability rates as well as other experience factors.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001639" name="syke:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationCapitalizedAmount" contextRef="C_0001010612_20191231" decimals="-3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001640" name="syke:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationCapitalizedAmount" contextRef="C_0001010612_20181231" decimals="-3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001641" name="syke:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationCapitalizedAmount" contextRef="C_0001010612_20201231" decimals="-3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> capitalized stock-based compensation costs as of December 31, 2020, 2019 and 2018.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2019<span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;"> </span>Equity Incentive Plan<span style="font-size:9pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;"> </span><span style="font-weight:normal;">&#8212; </span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">The Company&#8217;s Board of Directors (the &#8220;Board&#8221;) adopted the Sykes Enterprises, Incorporated 2019 Equity Incentive Plan (the "2019 Plan&#8221;) on March 12, 2019.&#160;&#160;The 2019 Plan was approved by the shareholders at the May 2019 annual shareholders meeting.&#160;&#160;The 2019 Plan replaced and superseded the Company&#8217;s 2011 Equity Incentive Plan (the &#8220;2011 Plan&#8221;). The outstanding awards granted under the 2011 Plan will remain in effect until their exercise, expiration or termination. The 2019 Plan provides for the grant of awards with respect to a maximum of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001642" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_sykeEquityIncentivePlanMember_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="6">4.0</ix:nonFraction> million shares of common stock, plus any shares of common stock that expire, terminate or are cancelled or forfeited under the terms of the 2011 Plan. The 2019 Plan permits the grant of restricted stock, stock appreciation rights, stock options and other stock-based awards to certain employees of, and certain non-employees who provide services to, the Company.</span>&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In the event of a change in control, except as may otherwise be provided in an award agreement, the outstanding 2019 Plan awards vesting upon the passage of time (e.g., employment-based) will be accelerated, and all awards vesting upon the attainment of performance goals will be deemed achieved at <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001643" name="syke:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardChangeInControlPerformanceBasedAwardVestingRightsPercentage" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_sykeRestrictedStockAndRestrictedStockUnitsRsuMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_sykeEquityIncentivePlanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">100</ix:nonFraction>% of target and all other restrictions applicable to outstanding awards will lapse, provided that the participant is employed by the Company on the date of the change in control.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Stock Appreciation Rights</span><span style="font-weight:bold;"> </span>&#8212; <span style="font-style:normal;">Stock-settled stock appreciation rights (&#8220;SARs&#8221;) represent the right to receive, without payment to the Company, a certain number of shares of common stock equal to the amount by which the fair market value of a share of common stock at the time of exercise exceeds the grant price.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The SARs are granted at the fair market value of the Company&#8217;s common stock on the date of the grant and vest <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001645" name="syke:ShareBasedCompensationSharesVestingPeriod" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapStockAppreciationRightsSARSMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_sykeEquityIncentivePlanMember_20200101_20201231">ratably over a three-year period following the date of grant</ix:nonNumeric>, provided the participant is employed by the Company on such date. The SARs have a term of <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001644" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardExpirationPeriod" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapStockAppreciationRightsSARSMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_sykeEquityIncentivePlanMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric> years from the date of grant. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">All currently outstanding SARs are exercisable within three months after the death, disability, retirement or termination of the participant&#8217;s employment with the Company, if and to the extent the SARs were exercisable immediately prior to such termination.&#160;&#160;If the participant&#8217;s employment is terminated for cause, or the participant terminates his or her own employment with the Company, any portion of the SARs not yet exercised (whether or not vested) terminates immediately on the date of termination of employment. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair value of each SAR is estimated on the date of grant using the Black-Scholes valuation model that uses various assumptions. The fair value of the SARs is expensed on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period. Expected volatility is based on the historical volatility of the Company&#8217;s stock. The risk-free rate for periods within the contractual life of the award is based on the yield curve of a zero-coupon U.S. Treasury bond on the date the award is granted with a maturity equal to the expected term of the award. Exercises and forfeitures are estimated within the </p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Restricted Shares and Restricted Stock Units</span><span style="font-weight:bold;"> &#8211; </span><span style="font-style:normal;">The Company awards performance and employment-based restricted shares (&#8220;restricted shares&#8221;) and/or restricted stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;) to eligible participants. The restricted shares are shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock (or in the case of RSUs, represent an equivalent number of shares of the </span></p>
</ix:continuation><p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">97</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" /><ix:continuation id="F_000439_dcnt_e7e79e14-1370-421c-b87f-03e26cd4c97b" continuedAt="F_000439_dcnt_5cc12d11-a793-479b-859a-96b33e0d949c">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-style:normal;">Company&#8217;s common stock) which are issued to the participant subject to (a) restrictions on transfer for a period of time and (b) forfeiture under certain conditions</span><span style="font-style:normal;">.</span><span style="font-style:normal;"> </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">For performance-based awards, the performance goals, including revenue growth and income from operations targets, provide a range of vesting possibilities from <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001689" name="syke:RangeOfVestingPossibilities" contextRef="C_0001010612_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_sykeRestrictedStockAndRestrictedStockUnitsRsuMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_sykeEquityIncentivePlanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">0</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001690" name="syke:RangeOfVestingPossibilities" contextRef="C_0001010612_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_sykeRestrictedStockAndRestrictedStockUnitsRsuMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_sykeEquityIncentivePlanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">100</ix:nonFraction>% and will be measured at the end of the three-year performance period. If the performance goals are met for the performance period, the shares will vest and all restrictions on the transfer of the restricted shares will lapse (or in the case of RSUs, an equivalent number of shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock will be issued to the recipient). The Company recognizes compensation cost, net of actual forfeitures, based on the fair value (which approximates the current market price) of the restricted shares and RSUs on the date of grant ratably over the requisite performance period based on the probability of achieving the performance goals. Changes in the probability of achieving the performance goals from period to period will result in corresponding changes in compensation expense.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Employment-based restricted shares and RSUs vest <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001691" name="syke:ShareBasedCompensationSharesVestingPeriod" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_sykeRestrictedStockAndRestrictedStockUnitsRsuMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_sykeEquityIncentivePlanMember_20200101_20201231">ratably over a three-year period following the date of grant</ix:nonNumeric>, provided the participant is employed by the Company on such date. The Company recognizes compensation cost, net of actual forfeitures, based on the fair value (which approximates the current market price) of the restricted shares and RSUs on the date of grant ratably over the requisite service period.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">If the participant&#8217;s employment with the Company is terminated for any reason, either by the Company or participant, prior to the date on which the restricted shares have vested and the restrictions have lapsed with respect to such vested shares, any restricted shares remaining subject to the restrictions (together with any dividends paid thereon) will be forfeited, unless there has been a change in control prior to such date.&#160;&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000527" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfNonvestedShareActivityTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_sykeRestrictedStockAndRestrictedStockUnitsRsuMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_sykeEquityIncentivePlanMember_20200101_20201231" escape="true">

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Non-Employee Director Compensation<span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;"> </span><span style="font-weight:normal;">&#8212; </span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">The Company does not have a formal, written compensation plan for non-employee directors.&#160;&#160;Subsequent to the expiration of its 2004 Non-Employee Director Fee Plan, the Board, upon recommendation of the Compensation Committee, determined that the Company&#8217;s non-employee directors would continue to receive a combination of cash and equity grants on an annual basis.&#160;&#160;The amount of the cash and equity </span></p>
</ix:continuation><p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">98</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">grants are determined annually by the Board, and the stock portion of such compensation is issued under the Company&#8217;s 2019 Plan</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Currently, all new non-employee directors joining the Board receive an initial grant of shares of common stock on the date the new director is elected or appointed, the number of which is determined by dividing $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001717" name="syke:ValueOfInitialGrantedSharesOfCommonStockToNewNonEmployeeDirector" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_sykeCommonStockAwardsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_sykeNonEmployeeDirectorCompensationMember_20201231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">60,000</ix:nonFraction> by the closing price of the Company&#8217;s common stock on the trading day immediately preceding the date a new director is elected or appointed, rounded to the nearest whole number of shares.&#160;&#160;The initial grant of shares vests in <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001718" name="syke:VestingPeriodOfInitialGrantedSharesOfCommonStockToNewNonEmployeeDirector" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_sykeCommonStockAwardsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_sykeNonEmployeeDirectorCompensationMember_20200101_20201231">twelve equal quarterly installments, one-twelfth on the date of grant and an additional one-twelfth on each successive third monthly anniversary of the date of grant.</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;&#160;The award lapses with respect to all unvested shares in the event the non-employee director ceases to be a director of the Company, and any unvested shares are forfeited.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Additionally, the current compensation structure approved by the Board, upon recommendation of the Compensation Committee, provides that each non-employee director receives, on the day after the annual shareholders meeting, an annual retainer for service as a non-employee director (the &#8220;Annual Retainer&#8221;). The total value of the Annual Retainer is $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001719" name="syke:ValueOfAnnualRetainerToNonEmployeeDirector" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_sykeCommonStockAwardsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_sykeNonEmployeeDirectorCompensationMember_20201231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">170,000</ix:nonFraction>, of which $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001720" name="syke:AnnualRetainerPayableInCashToNonEmployeeDirector" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_sykeCommonStockAwardsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_sykeNonEmployeeDirectorCompensationMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">70,000</ix:nonFraction> is payable in cash, and the remainder is paid in stock, the amount of which is determined by dividing $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001721" name="syke:AnnualRetainerPayableInStockToNonEmployeeDirector" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_sykeCommonStockAwardsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_sykeNonEmployeeDirectorCompensationMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">100,000</ix:nonFraction> by the closing price of the Company&#8217;s common stock on the date of the annual shareholders&#8217; meeting.&#160;&#160;The annual grant of shares paid to non-employee directors vests in <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001722" name="syke:VestingPeriodOfAnnualGrantedSharesOfCommonStockToNonEmployeeDirector" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_sykeCommonStockAwardsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_sykeNonEmployeeDirectorCompensationMember_20200101_20201231">four equal quarterly installments, one-fourth on the date of grant and an additional one-fourth on each successive third monthly anniversary of the date of grant</ix:nonNumeric>). The award lapses with respect to all unpaid cash and unvested shares in the event the non-employee director ceases to be a director of the Company, and any unvested shares and unpaid cash are forfeited.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000529" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfNonvestedShareActivityTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_sykeCommonStockAwardsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_sykeNonEmployeeDirectorCompensationMember_20200101_20201231" escape="true">

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 25. Segments and Geographic Information</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000471" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001010612_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company operates within <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_sykeRegion" id="F_001801" name="us-gaap:NumberOfOperatingSegments" contextRef="C_0001010612_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">two</ix:nonFraction> regions, the Americas and EMEA. Each region represents a reportable segment comprised of aggregated regional operating segments, which portray similar economic characteristics. The Company aligns its business into <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_sykeSegment" id="F_001802" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportableSegments" contextRef="C_0001010612_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">two</ix:nonFraction> segments to effectively manage the business and support the customer care needs of every client and to respond to the demands of the Company&#8217;s global customers. </p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The reportable segments consist of (1)&#160;the Americas, which includes the United States, Canada, Latin America, Australia and the Asia Pacific Rim, and provides outsourced customer experience management solutions (with an emphasis on inbound multichannel demand generation, customer service and technical support) and technical staffing, and (2)&#160;EMEA, which includes Europe, the Middle East and Africa, and provides outsourced customer experience management solutions (with an emphasis on technical support and customer service) and fulfillment services. The Company also provides a suite of solutions such as RPA consulting, implementation, hosting and managed services that optimizes its differentiated full lifecycle management services platform. The sites within Latin America, Australia and the Asia Pacific Rim are included in the Americas segment given the nature of the business and client profile, which is primarily made up of U.S.-based companies that are using the Company&#8217;s services in these locations to support their customer experience management needs. </p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000535" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfSegmentReportingInformationBySegmentTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001010612_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000535_dcnt_ef030256-13e6-4989-92af-bec0a3f7cf4d">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 27. Related Party Transactions </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_001989" name="us-gaap:RelatedPartyTransactionDescriptionOfTransaction" contextRef="C_0001010612_us-gaapRelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis_us-gaapImmediateFamilyMemberOfManagementOrPrincipalOwnerMember_20200101_20201231">In January 2008, the Company entered into a lease for a customer experience management center located in Kingstree, South Carolina. The landlord, Kingstree Office One, LLC, is an entity controlled by John H. Sykes, the founder, former Chairman and former Chief Executive Officer of the Company and the father of Charles Sykes, President and Chief Executive Officer of the Company.
